title: The specified geometric field evaluation comparison preserves bounded coefficient scalars
statement: Let ell be prime and i:K -> Kprime an arbitrary embedding of algebraically closed fields. For every actual module M over the condensed bounded coefficient ring on Spec(K) and every scalar r in Qbar_ell, the specified abelian evaluation comparison commutes with multiplication by r on M and on its inverse-image module computed by restriction along the inverse coefficient isomorphism. This is an equality for the already specified abelian comparison, not an existence statement for a module comparison.

source.place: Section 4, finite-matrix refinement: presentation and geometric-fibre comparison after coefficient realization (steps 1--3)

proof.text: The canonical abelian evaluation comparison is the inverse-image adjunction unit followed by restriction along the terminal-object comparison. Monoidality of the adjunction unit and tensor naturality of restriction identify the source module action with the evaluated inverse-image action, transporting coefficients by the canonical evaluated coefficient map.

source.place: Section 4, finite-matrix refinement: presentation and geometric-fibre comparison after coefficient realization (steps 1--3)

proof.text: Precompose the coefficient square with globalCoefficientIso and the invertible bounded-presheaf unit at the terminal object. Every bounded function on a field spectrum is constant. The normalized profinite-test formula globalCoefficientIso_test identifies its pullback with the same constant. Cancel fieldUnitIso and evaluate by boundedPointIso. Surjectivity proves the coefficient square.

proof.text: Restriction along the inverse of condensedPullbackHom cancels the coefficient transport. Apply the constructed ordinary module action and restriction through ULift to the tensor-action identity. This gives exactly the displayed equality for every scalar and every module.
